title: vToken: Token-Level Virtualization for Reclaimable KV Caches
abstract: arXiv:2608.13263v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language model serving faces a critical memory bottleneck: the KV cache grows with sequence length and batch size. PagedAttention uses fixed-size memory blocks to reduce allocator-level fragmentation, but recent KV eviction algorithms operate at a token granularity finer than block-level management. This mismatch causes intra-block fragmentation, leaving a large fraction of allocated KV memory unreclaimable. We present vToken, a lightweight token-level virtualization layer that decouples logical token liveness from physical block placement. vToken maintains a stable logical token view through token-table indirection and realizes physical reclamation by repacking live tokens asynchronously. The design preserves PagedAttention kernels and CUDA Graph compatibility. We implement vToken in vLLM and evaluate it with H2O, Random, and Scissorhands across models. Compared with a paired Naive-Evict baseline, vToken reduces retained KV blocks

translated_title: vToken：面向可回收KV缓存的分词级虚拟化技术
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.13263v1 公告类型：新 摘要：大型语言模型服务面临一个关键的内存瓶颈：KV缓存随序列长度和批处理大小增长。PagedAttention使用固定大小的内存块来减少分配器层面的碎片，但最近的KV淘汰算法在比块级管理更细的分词粒度上运行。这种不匹配导致块内碎片，使得大量已分配的KV内存无法回收。我们提出了vToken，一种轻量级的分词级虚拟化层，它将逻辑分词的活跃性与物理块的放置解耦。vToken通过分词表间接寻址维护稳定的逻辑分词视图，并通过异步重打包活跃分词实现物理回收。该设计保留了PagedAttention内核和CUDA Graph兼容性。我们在vLLM中实现了vToken，并使用H2O、Random和Scissorhands在多个模型上进行了评估。与配对的Naive-Evict基线相比，vToken减少了保留的KV块数量。
tldr: vToken通过引入分词级虚拟化层，解耦逻辑活跃性与物理块放置，并采用异步重打包机制，有效解决了KV缓存中块内碎片导致的不可回收问题，从而显著减少内存占用。
en_tdlr: vToken introduces a token-level virtualization layer that decouples logical liveness from physical block placement and uses asynchronous repacking, effectively resolving intra-block fragmentation in KV caches to significantly reduce memory usage.
